findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS
Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole batch
Reminders already scheduled with Twilio can be counted as failures and deleted
Use atomic increment and extract the duplicated retry threshold logic
Unindexed `retryCount` predicate in an OR forces a table scan on every cron run

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate: Non-atomic increment of retryCount - retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 is a read-modify-write on a stale value, so if two cron invocations overlap, increments are lost; should use Prisma's { increment: 1 } instead
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same problem as the golden comment: the non-atomic increment of retryCount using `reminder.retryCount + 1` which reads a stale value and can lose increments under concurrent execution. Both recommend using Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` as the solution. The only minor difference is the golden comment also mentions the catch block has the same issue, but the core problem identified is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Retry-count cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS - the new OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } has no method filter, so the SMS cron job will delete any WorkflowReminder whose retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same bug as the golden comment: the retryCount > 1 condition in the deletion logic lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to delete all reminder types (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) instead of only SMS reminders. Both comments point to the same underlying problem with the same technical details.

false_positives.candidate: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole batch - prisma.workflowReminder.update inside catch is not protected and can throw (P2025 if reminder was deleted concurrently, or on DB connectivity error), causing remaining reminders to go unprocessed and returning a 500

Reminders already scheduled with Twilio can be counted as failures and deleted - if twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the later update that sets scheduled: true and referenceId throws, the reminder is counted as failed and retryCount is incremented, leading to duplicate messages and lost referenceId
Duplicated retry threshold logic with magic number - the cutoff gt: 1 is a magic number allowing only two failed attempts before silent deletion, and the update logic is duplicated in two places

Unindexed retryCount predicate in an OR forces a table scan on every cron run - Postgres cannot satisfy the OR condition from existing indexes, causing full table scans on the potentially large WorkflowReminder table
